metas.name: Cuverville Island
metas.note: Cuverville Island can be recognised by the overcast weather combined with the coastline to the northwest. You’ll also see a decent number of penguins, particularly toward the east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Danco Island
metas.note: Danco Island can be recognised by the beautiful sunset coverage over a snowy fjord.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Dark soil
metas.note: The soil will always be dark.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Deception Island Bay
metas.note: The Deception Island Bay can be recognized by the blue and white ship in the bay, and the abandoned equipment on the beach.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Deception Island black sand beach
metas.note: A beach with black sand and many penguins can be seen on Deception Island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Deception Island trekker walking in a line
metas.note: The trekker can be seen walking in a line on Deception Island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Half Moon Island
metas.note: Half Moon Island was covered by a tripod. It can also be recognized by the numerous other people in red jackets.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: McMurdo Station
metas.note:
McMurdo Station is the largest research station on Antarctica, and can be recognized by the dark brown soil, many buildings, American infrastructure and sunset coverage.

NOTE: A lot of the coverage around McMurdo Station has the sun setting in the south, which shouldn’t lead you to guess in the northern hemisphere.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: McMurdo Station - Eastern side wooden cabin
metas.note: On the eastern side of McMurdo Station you can find a small wooden cabin, having a tripod going inside.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: McMurdo Station - Ice trekker
metas.note: Southeast of McMurdo station, the trekker can be seen walking on a layer of ice around various machinery.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: McMurdo Station - Inside tripod
metas.note: You can also find tripod coverage inside several buildings at McMurdo Station.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: McMurdo Station - South landscape
metas.note: A vast, snowy landscape with spread out hills can be seen south of McMurdo station.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Penguins
metas.note:
Penguins can be found on parts of the coverage.

NOTE: This is mostly useful to exclude coverage in the Arctics.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Petermann Island
metas.note: Petermann Island can be recognized by the layer of snow with patches of exposed rocks, and the overexposed camera.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Ross Island - Dark and barren rocky soil
metas.note: The coverage at the western tip of Ross Island can typically be recognised by the extremely dark, and mostly barren, rocky soil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Ross Island - Western landscape
metas.note: The trekker can be seen walking through a fantastical landscape consisting of many desolate valleys on mainland Antarctica, west of Ross Island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Ross Island - Wooden cabin
metas.note: A tripod featuring the exterior and interior of a small wooden cabin with a grey metal roof can be found south of the eastern tip of Ross Island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Snow and ice
metas.note: Most of Antarctica is covered in snow and ice.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: South Pole flags
metas.note:
The tripod at the south pole can be recognized by numerous countries’ flags around the tripod, and a sign with ‘Geographic South Pole’ written on it.

This location is often on community-made world maps for a better scoring range.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: South Pole observatory
metas.note: The South Pole Observatory has tripod coverage going around and inside of it.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.
